question: Why do standard real-estate appraisal frameworks split valuation into cost, sales-comparison, and income approaches instead of one canonical value, and which should dominate for a given asset class?
summary: Derived from cheapest-substitute pricing that the three approaches map to three distinct substitution markets (build/resell/capitalize income), with dominance set by which market has liquid data per asset class; matches standard appraisal doctrine almost exactly. One extension (cost/income gap as a supply-arbitrage leading indicator) did not surface in the corpus search.
